The functional adapter has been implemented correctly as described in Section 3.3, as a learnable down projection layer, then a ReLU function, then a learnable up projection layer
The encoder of the representation descriptor is implemented as a linear layer that projects to 128 dimensions
LeakyReLU is applied to the output of the encoder of the representation descriptor
The decoder of the representation descriptor is implemented as a linear layer that projects from 128 dimensions back to the original dimensionality
The router has been implemented as a linear mapping function (using a learnable matrix) followed by a softmax operation
The output of the second normalization layer (after the first normalization layer, then multi-head self-attention, then residual connection) is used as input for the representation
A linear combination of the outputs of the functional adapters is computed, with the weights corresponding to the output of the router
A linear combination of the outputs of the functional adapters is added to the output of the fully connected layer and the residual layer in the transformer block to produce the ou

The average incremental accuracy $\bar{A}$ is computed as $\bar{A} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{t=1}^N A_t$, where $A_t$ is the average accuracy on all seen tasks after training on the $t$-
All adapters are trained for 5 epochs.
The representation descriptors are trained for 20 epochs.
The batch size is 32.
SGD is used as the optimizer.
The initial learning rate is set to 0.005 for adapters.
The initial learning rate is set to 0.01 for representational descriptors.
The learning rate decays with cosine annealing.
Self-expansion is only enabled in the last three transformer layers.
The adapters in SEMA and ADAM project down to a dimensionality of 48
